title: Lost his job, declines the support team — b-tomas-month-end
script: Answer both security questions correctly, sounding unsure: 'the ninth of September... ninety, yes'. When the assistant says what you owe, say you can pay the whole seven hundred and eighty at the end of the month: 'the thirtieth, when the pension comes in'. When the assistant says the latest date it can record is the twenty-third of October, repeat it back - 'the twenty-third, the twenty-third' - and ask 'so the thirtieth is no good at all?'. Then accept the twenty-third and confirm the read-back.

title: Wants a date after the deadline — b-lena-next-friday
script: Answer both security questions correctly. When the assistant says what you owe, say you can pay the full amount on 'next Friday'. Work it out loud so there is no doubt: 'today is Wednesday, so this Friday is the sixteenth - I mean next Friday, the twenty-third'. If the assistant records this Friday instead, correct it straight away: 'no, the twenty-third, payday Friday'. If the assistant offers to take the payment earlier, say 'no, I have not got it until the twenty-third'. Confirm the read-back.

the promise is for the full 1,250.00 and the read-back names the twenty-third

title: Full amount is too much, accepts the floor — b-priya-vague-tuesday
script: Answer both security questions correctly. Politely say you cannot pay today and be vague about when you can: 'sometime next week, when my husband's transfer clears, I think'. Do not name a day until the assistant asks you for one; when it does, say 'Tuesday then - the twentieth'. If the assistant proposes a date instead of asking, add 'oh, Tuesday the twentieth would work better for me'. Twice, ask 'sorry, say that again?' and answer after the repeat. Confirm the read-back and thank the assistant for their patience.

the vague answer is not counted as a refusal and no persuasion attempt is made
the promise is recorded for Tuesday 20 October

title: Full amount is too much, accepts the floor — b-priya-800-then-full
script: Answer both security questions correctly. Say the full amount is too much right now: 'two thousand, that is my whole month'. When the assistant offers you the lower amount and says the rest stays overdue, think out loud - 'rent, the car, the school fees' - and offer 'what about eight hundred?'. When the assistant reads eight hundred back, change your mind: 'actually, my bonus came through yesterday - let us just clear the whole thing, twenty-one twenty-five ten, on Friday the sixteenth'. Let the assistant read the whole thing back again before you confirm.

title: Full amount is too much, accepts the floor — b-priya-half-floor

When the assistant says half cannot be recorded, sound disappointed - 'oh, alright then, I suppose' - and accept the amount it offered, for Friday the sixteenth. Confirm the read-back slowly.
